units.function: Diagnoses Paperclip storage configuration. local_disk resolves and creates the base directory, then checks W_OK; the alternative branch requires non-empty S3 bucket and region but deliberately skips reachability and returns a warning.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI doctor leaf -> Paperclip storage config and runtime-path alias -> direct local filesystem operations. The S3 branch performs string checks only and does not call the storage provider abstraction, AWS SDK or service. It is coupled to local_disk/S3 configuration shapes but not to artifact domain models.
units.keyDataModels: Storage provider, local baseDir, S3 bucket and region, and free-form CheckResult. No object namespace/prefix, tenant, artifact/evidence class, digest, encryption key, retention/legal hold, quota, replication, lifecycle, endpoint/account or stable diagnostic code is represented.
units.lifecycle: Local: resolve path -> recursively create when absent -> synchronously test W_OK -> pass/fail. S3: trim bucket/region -> fail missing values -> otherwise always warn that reachability was skipped. There is no test-object put/get/delete round trip, capacity/latency check, cleanup, timeout, credential validation or data-integrity verification.
units.testAssessment: No focused storageCheck test was found. CLI TypeScript checking passes. The earlier completed local storage-provider test assessment proved actual disk I/O in the server provider and was reused without rereading, but it does not exercise this doctor wrapper or cover traversal/symlinks, ranges, streaming, digests, atomicity, concurrency, permissions, quotas, encryption, retention or S3 parity. This check's mkdir failures, read-only/full storage, custom paths and S3 invalid/policy cases remain untested.
units.designRationale: The check avoids making a potentially billable/destructive S3 request during a generic doctor run and catches common local setup errors cheaply. That conservative S3 behavior is preferable to implicit cloud writes, but directory writability and non-empty strings are configuration hints rather than storage readiness.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must store artifacts and responsibility evidence across managed cloud and local enterprise profiles with tenant isolation, authorization, integrity, provenance, retention, legal hold, encryption, quota, backup/restore and verifiable lifecycle semantics.
units.companyOsFit: Reimplement via an Event/Data/Audit storage capability contract. Static checks should validate structured provider policy without network or mutation; an explicit authorized self-test may perform a bounded namespaced write/read/digest/delete round trip with cost and cleanup evidence. Operational artifacts and immutable responsibility evidence require distinct classes and guarantees even when they share a physical provider.
units.responsibilityConflict: A writable directory does not prove that evidence is immutable, attributable or retained. Silent directory creation lacks an accountable operator/action record. S3 bucket presence also says nothing about which human, Agent, tenant or Connector may read/write objects, so neither result can satisfy the Company OS responsibility chain.

units.securityFindings: Local baseDir is recursively created before the try/catch without allowed-root, symlink, owner, mode or parent-directory checks; creation errors escape. W_OK does not prove safe object creation, atomic writes, service-user access, capacity, quota, mount durability or actual provider behavior. The full path is disclosed. S3 validates only non-empty bucket/region and does not check endpoint/account ownership, credentials, least privilege, TLS, public-access block, encryption/KMS, versioning, object lock, tenant prefix policy, residency or reachability. Bucket and region are exposed in output.
